newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GOVERNMENT OVERSPENDING UNDER FIRE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GOVERNMENT OVERSPENDING UNDER FIRE.

text.p: South African opposition parties on Friday took advantage of a parliament debate on the Adjustments Appropriation Bill to take the African National Congress government to task on several perceived policy errors.
The bill, which provides for a 2.4 billion rand increase in the 19967/97 budget to 176.1 billion rand, detailed overspending in all government departments.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel allowed legislators to ask query every cabinet minister, and some were sharply criticised.

Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo bore most of the flak in a lively and sometimes acrimonious debate for the extra 177 million rand provided for the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC).

The National Party (NP), which blatantly used the SABC as a propaganda tool during the apartheid era, said the state broadcaster was now being used by the ANC for its own ends and badly managed by over-paid political appointees.
As a result, hundreds of employees were being retrenched, services had deteriorated -- especially for Afrikaans speakers -- and its increasing losses had to be paid for by taxpayers.

Naidoo made a spirited defence of the SABC, saying the NP had created "a monster" that now needed to be restructured to meet the needs of all South Africans and to bring it in line with international standards.
Most ministers were criticised because they had to roll over millions of rands in their 1996/97 budgets to the next financial year.
When the health, policing and housing needs of the country were so great, it was inexcusable that funds had not been used, opposition legislators said.

The ministers explained it was not always possible to use all funds allocated to projects in one year, especially if long lead times involved. Manuel said the necessary management systems were not yet in place in some departments to ensure that funds were well spent.
Unspent allocations in all government departments totalled 12 billion rand, of which they had been allowed to keep 8.9 billion rand.
Manuel said the move to multi-year budgeting would help do away with the problem of roll overs and "we will be able to match policy with spending much more easily".
The bill was eventually passed despite the objections of the minority parties and will now go to the new Council of Provinces for final approval.
